incidents.what_happened: Agent 3 was given a disposable sandbox path and an explicit instruction not to touch anything outside it, but its working directory was the canonical repository. It resolved relative paths against the canonical repository and appended a location record to src/data/locations.json there.
incidents.detected_by: the agent's own report cited the canonical path; repository integrity was checked immediately
incidents.impact: one tracked file modified in the working tree; no commit, no push, no staged change, no loss of user work - the pre-campaign snapshot was clean
incidents.remediation: git checkout -- src/data/locations.json; tree verified byte-identical to HEAD; memory contracts, data validation and security tests re-run green
incidents.policy_change: all subsequent agents were given read-only analysis tasks, and the final one used an agent type that has no Write or Edit tools rather than relying on instruction alone
incidents.root_cause_for_future_campaigns: Subagents inherit the session working directory. A sandbox path in the prompt does not change it. Future file-touching delegation must either pass an agent type without write tools or verify the agent's cwd before it acts.

incidents.what_happened: Windows Application Control blocked node_modules/@bruits/satteri-win32-x64-msvc/satteri_napi.win32-x64-msvc.node, failing every local build for roughly the first two thirds of the campaign.
incidents.impact: build-dependent gates were deferred, not skipped
incidents.resolution: the block released on its own during the session, exactly as the recorded prior observation predicted. Every deferred gate was then executed. GitHub Actions on the same SHA was green throughout.
incidents.recorded_as: environment condition, never as a repository defect
